alkalab.title: Alkalab
alkalab.description: Alkalab is a powder-sand chemistry lab that runs in the browser, written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly.
alkalab.aria_label: Alkalab sandbox. Drag to paint, right-click to erase, Space to pause, S to step, C to clear, Ctrl+Z to undo, X for the boom tool.
alkalab.hint: Drag to paint · right-click to erase · Space pause · S step · C clear · Ctrl+Z undo · X boom tool

status.runtime_failed: Unable to load the lab runtime

notes: One flat buffer: the grid is a single Vec<Cell>, (x, y) maps to y * width + x, and a one-cell inert border removes every bounds check.
Bottom-up ticks: rows scan bottom to top so falling material cannot update twice, and the column direction flips each frame so water has no favourite side.
Density, not special cases: sand sinks in water, oil floats on it, and mercury sinks through both, all from one comparison.
Zero-copy pixels: Rust renders straight into a Uint8ClampedArray view of wasm memory, so nothing crosses the boundary per frame.
Declarative chemistry: 2 Na + 2 H2O -> 2 NaOH + H2, CaC2 + 2 H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + C2H2, and lava + sand -> glass are single table rows.

overview.label: Minecraft Mod
overview.title: A whole new layer of survival
overview.text: Built primarily with Java and Kotlin, SupremeMC expands every stage of the game, from new ores and gear in the Overworld to custom dimensions, structures, and creatures. The latest version ships for both Fabric and NeoForge from a single shared codebase.

gear.title: Tools, Weapons & Armor
gear.text: New materials with full tool and armor sets, plus specialty weapons with their own behavior.

mobs.title: Creatures
mobs.text: New hostile and passive mobs that bring fresh threats and wildlife to the world.

worlds.title: Dimensions & Biomes
worlds.text: Custom dimensions and hand-tuned biomes with their own terrain, trees, and vegetation.

structures.title: Structures & Blocks
structures.text: Hundreds of new building blocks alongside generated structures to explore in the Nether and the End.

explosives.title: Explosives
explosives.text: Specialty TNT variants that do more than just blow things up.

magic.title: Enchantments & Potions
magic.text: New enchantments and brewable potions that add depth to combat, mining, and exploration.

build.label: Engineering
build.title: How it's built
build.text: The current release uses a MultiLoader architecture: gameplay code lives in a shared common module compiled against vanilla Minecraft, while thin Fabric and NeoForge modules load it into each platform. Recipes, models, tags, and translations are produced with data generators to keep hundreds of assets consistent.

timeline.text: SupremeMC is born, introducing its first custom ores, tools, and armor.
Ported forward on Forge as the mod grows into a large content pack with new mobs, dimensions, and structures.
Updated for 1.21 alongside companion SupremeMC enchantment and wood-cutting data packs.
Rebuilt on a MultiLoader template to ship on both Fabric and NeoForge from one codebase.

rustcraft.title: Rustcraft
rustcraft.description: Rustcraft is a lightweight Minecraft-style voxel game written from scratch in Rust. Built on winit for windowing and wgpu for rendering rather than a full game engine, it owns its world, meshing and physics code, and grows an infinite noise-generated world of hills, cliffs, oceans and caves on the desktop.

gallery.label: Screenshots
gallery.title: From inside the world
gallery.text: Every chunk is generated from multi-octave Perlin noise, carved by Minecraft Beta's own cave and ravine carvers, then meshed and lit as it streams in around the player.

world.alt: A Rustcraft landscape of rolling grass hills, cliffs and a translucent ocean under a bright sky
world.caption: Rolling hills, cliffs and translucent oceans stream in around the player.

caves.alt: A Rustcraft cave network glowing with the light of a lava pool below the surface
caves.caption: Cave and ravine carvers worm through the rock, pooling as lava at the bottom of the world.

house.alt: A small wooden Rustcraft house built on a grass hillside
house.caption: Break and place blocks to build, then stock the hotbar from a creative inventory.

world.title: Infinite world
world.text: An infinite, noise-generated world of rolling hills, cliffs, overhangs and oceans, streamed in chunks around the player on worker threads.

terrain.title: Carved terrain
terrain.text: Minecraft Beta's own cave and ravine carvers cut networks of ellipsoids through the rock, and anything still open at lava level becomes a glowing lava sea.

lighting.title: Deferred lighting
lighting.text: The world renders into a G-buffer and is lit in one fullscreen pass: baked per-corner sky light with smooth lighting and ambient occlusion, plus a real sun shadow map.

building.title: Build & explore
building.text: A first-person fly camera where right-click breaks and left-click places, backed by a creative inventory of blocks you open with E.

build.label: Engineering
build.title: How it's built
build.text: Rustcraft owns its world, meshing and physics code outright. Chunks are generated on worker threads while the frame loop keeps drawing, meshed with cross-chunk hidden-face culling, and drawn from individual PNGs in a texture_2d_array, so there is no engine sitting between the code and the GPU.
